account:
Today I have kept my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, lunch at home, council letters, and tea with my neighbour. I have now returned to the office at 16:40, ten minutes after my scheduled return; secretary and freight are here. An eighteen o'clock community gathering with the innkeeper is scheduled in the great hall, and freight has offered to escort me there. I understand it as a community gathering, but do not yet know its particular business.

The unusual feature today is repeated, vague talk about a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Townsfolk repeated it near the mill, sometimes naming baker and freight as having been there. This is hearsay, not evidence of a proposal or decision. Secretary's enquiries found no firsthand proposal evidence, and neighbour likewise reported no firsthand sign of any change. I do not know whether the rumours concern any genuine plan or what such a plan would be for. I have asked that actual evidence and new correspondence come to the office, keeping rumours separate from facts.

Council recordkeeping remains unresolved: secretary has located neither an accounts ledger nor the usual incoming-correspondence deposit or responsible keeper. The known office records contain appointment books and secretary's report. No correspondence requiring my decision has been reported. At the mill I counted eighty-two hay bales in the sales chest, but received no responsible worker's condition report, so I cannot treat the count as a completed assessment of the grain's condition. Tea was cordial; neighbour described a pleasant stroll and town conversation, with no confirmed bridge or port news.
